newsitem.title: UK: UK new construction orders up 1.0% in 3mths to May.
newsitem.headline: UK new construction orders up 1.0% in 3mths to May.

text.p: The total volume of new orders received by construction contractors in Britain in the three months to May was one percent higher compared with the previous three months, the Department of Environment said on Thursday.

New orders were six percent up on the same three months a year ago. The total volume of construction new orders fell sharply in May itself, to their lowest level for nearly a year, the DoE said. In current prices the total value of new orders in May was 1,904 million stg.
The increase over the latest three months was mainly due to large increases in the private commercial and public housing sectors.
New orders in the private housing sector in the three months to May were 20 percent lower compared with the previous three months and one percent lower than in the corresponding period a year ago.
Public housing and housing association orders in the latest three months were 45 percent higher than in the previous three months and 18 percent higher than a year earlier.
Infrastructure orders in the latest three months were two percent lower compared with the previous three months and four percent lower than a year ago.

Public non-housing orders (excluding infrastructure) in the latest three months were six percent higher compared with the previous three months but 12 percent lower than in the corresponding period a year ago.

Private industrial orders in the latest three months were unchanged compared with the previous three months but 28 percent higher than a year ago. Private commercial orders in the latest three months were 12 percent higher compared with the previous three months and 17 percent higher than in the corresponding period a year ago.
